title: About
text:
I am a theoretical physicist from Tineo, Asturias, currently based in Barcelona. My academic path has taken me through Oviedo, Madrid, Waterloo, Leuven, Amsterdam, Bariloche, CERN and Barcelona.
Most of my work is driven by a simple question: which features of gravity and quantum field theory are genuinely universal, and which depend on the particular language or model we use to describe them?
Beyond physics, I have also pursued undergraduate studies in Economics through UNED.

title: Research
text: My research sits at the intersection of gravitation, black-hole physics, quantum field theory, holography and quantum information. A recurring theme is the search for structures that remain simple or universal even when one moves beyond the most familiar theories.

title: Research
text:
Black holes
A substantial part of my work concerns the structure and dynamics of black holes, particularly when the gravitational dynamics differs from Einstein’s theory. Topics include regular black holes, gravitational collapse, the internal structure of black holes, extremal and near-extremal limits, echoes and compact objects, and the role of higher-curvature corrections in singularity resolution.

title: Research
text:
Higher-curvature gravity
I have worked extensively on Einsteinian cubic gravity and on the broader families of generalized quasi-topological gravities. These theories contain higher powers of the curvature while retaining unusually simple equations in physically important sectors. This makes it possible to investigate black holes, cosmology, holography and effective-field-theory questions in settings much richer than General Relativity but still analytically tractable.

title: Research
text:
Entanglement in quantum field theory
A second major line of work uses entanglement and information-theoretic quantities to probe the structure of quantum field theories. This includes universal contributions to entanglement entropy, singular and deformed entangling surfaces, mutual and multipartite information, reflected entropy, and bounds on CFT data derived from entanglement constraints.

title: Research
text:
Holography and quantum gravity
Holography provides a bridge between these directions. I have used gravitational theories to study entanglement and CFT observables, and conversely quantum-information ideas to constrain gravitational dynamics. Related work concerns generalized symmetries, holographic entanglement entropy, geometric functionals and aspects of quantum gravity.

title: Pablo Bueno
text:
Theoretical physics · Gravitation · Quantum field theory




I am a theoretical physicist and Professor Agregat at the Institute of Cosmos Sciences of the University of Barcelona (ICCUB). I work on black holes, gravitational theories beyond General Relativity, quantum field theory, entanglement and holography.


Professor Agregat · Universitat de Barcelona ICCUB Barcelona


Research Publications People

title: Pablo Bueno
text:
Research



Black holes


Regular black holes, collapse, interiors, extremality and the fate of spacetime singularities.

 

Higher-curvature gravity


Einsteinian cubic gravity, generalized quasi-topological gravities and related extensions of General Relativity.

 

Entanglement in quantum field theory


Entanglement entropy, mutual information and universal constraints on quantum and conformal field theories.

 

Holography and quantum gravity


Holographic entanglement, geometry, generalized symmetries and quantum aspects of gravity.
